description: Historical evidence behind a crypto opportunity: for its strategy (and coin where enough samples exist) the measured populations — detected, blocked, published, expired without entry, completed, wins, losses, time exits — plus win rate over completed outcomes only with a Wilson interval, average/median/total net return, distinct days and coins, ML model evidence status and the measurement window. Real measurements, never fabricated; short windows have wide error bars. Paid per request.

signal_id.description: Signal id, e.g. 'sig_a1b2c3d4e5f6'; returns the measured track record of its strategy (win rate over completed outcomes only, with Wilson interval).

name: get_crypto_evidence

checked_at.description: When we produced this answer (ISO 8601, UTC). The only ISO timestamp in the payload; every other timestamp is unix seconds.

coin.description: Coin the evidence is scoped to; null means too few coin-level samples, so the numbers are strategy-wide.

disclaimer.description: Our product boundary, verbatim in every paid advice response: market intelligence only, no execution, no custody, no position sizing, and opportunity_score is a heuristic rather than a calibrated win probability.

measured_since.description: Unix seconds — start of the measurement window.

metrics.description: Measured over completed outcomes only (WIN + LOSS + TIME). Anything the source cannot compute is null — never fabricated.

avg_net_return_maker_pct.description: Mean net return assuming passive maker fills; optimistic, because a maker fill is never guaranteed.

avg_net_return_pct.description: Mean net return per completed outcome in percent, after taker costs. Can be negative.

completed_sample_count.description: Sample size behind every metric below; small samples mean wide Wilson bounds — read them.

distinct_coins.description: Distinct coins contributing completed outcomes; low values mean the sample is concentrated in one market.

distinct_days.description: Distinct calendar days contributing completed outcomes; low values mean the sample is clustered in time.

median_net_return_pct.description: Median net return per completed outcome in percent; less outlier-sensitive than the mean.

total_net_return_pct.description: Sum of net returns over all completed outcomes in percent — not a compounded account return.

wilson_high_pct.description: Upper bound of the 95% Wilson score interval around win_rate_pct.

wilson_low_pct.description: Lower bound of the 95% Wilson score interval around win_rate_pct; the conservative read.

win_definition.description: How a win is counted; currently always 'net_return_gt_0' — net return after costs above zero, so a profitable TIME exit counts as a win even though it is not in populations.wins.

win_rate_pct.description: Percentage of COMPLETED outcomes that were profitable; denominator is completed (WIN+LOSS+TIME), never detected or published.

ml_models.description: Machine-learning models used by this strategy and how far their own validation has come.

evidence_status.description: How far out-of-sample validation has come. UNVALIDATED = no measured outcomes yet, EARLY_EVIDENCE = too few to lean on, VALIDATED = enough measured evidence, REJECTED = measured and found not to work.

sample_count.description: Measured outcomes behind this evidence_status; 0 means nothing has been validated yet.

note.description: Verbatim upstream note on how populations and metrics relate; states that win rate and returns use completed outcomes only.

populations.description: Disjoint counts over the window, reported apart from the metrics so selection effects stay visible. blocked and expired_without_entry are EXCLUDED from every metric denominator.

blocked.description: Candidates blocked internally upstream (never traded); excluded from all metric denominators.

completed.description: Entered positions with a finished outcome (WIN, LOSS or TIME); the denominator of win_rate_pct and the return metrics.

detected.description: Candidates the strategy detected, before internal filtering.

expired_without_entry.description: Published candidates whose entry window closed without a fill; excluded from all metric denominators.

losses.description: Exit-status count of positions that exited on their stop.

pending.description: Entered positions still open; no outcome yet, so counted nowhere in metrics.

time_exits.description: Exit-status count of positions closed because the holding horizon ran out; a profitable one still counts as a win in win_rate_pct.

wins.description: Exit-status count of positions that exited on their target — a count of exit REASON, not of profitability (see metrics.win_definition).

query.description: The validated input echoed back, i.e. the signal_id you asked for.

signal_id.description: Stable id of the opportunity across versions; the input for every other call in the chain.

recommended_next_call.description: Machine-readable next step in the chain (scan → signal → validate → evidence → check), so you can follow the workflow without documentation. null means there is explicitly nothing useful to call now; next_check_after then says when to come back.

arguments.description: Arguments to pass verbatim, e.g. {"signal_id":"sig_a1b2c3d4e5f6"}, plus known_version for check_crypto_signal.

reason.description: Why this is the useful next step, in plain language.

tool.description: Name of the MCP tool to call next.

source_as_of.description: Unix seconds — freshness of the upstream advice system's answer.

source_disclaimer.description: Verbatim disclaimer of the upstream advice system, passed through unedited.

strategy.description: Strategy version the evidence is scoped to, e.g. 'momentum-breakout-v1'.

strategy_evidence_status.description: How far out-of-sample validation has come. UNVALIDATED = no measured outcomes yet, EARLY_EVIDENCE = too few to lean on, VALIDATED = enough measured evidence, REJECTED = measured and found not to work.

window_days.description: Length of the measurement window in days.
